post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and

    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

# Outcome sub-dossier — realized record of the RLJ Lodging Trust / FelCor combination, ~3-5-year horizon (~2020-2022)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. FelCor Lodging Trust Incorporated deregistered at
> closing and files no periodic reports of its own; the acquirer, RLJ Lodging Trust,
> remains a continuing SEC registrant, so this sub-dossier draws on RLJ's later Form
> 10-K filings. It contains no information about how the transaction was structured at
> closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- FelCor Lodging Trust Incorporated filed a Form 15 certifying termination of Exchange
  Act registration on September 8, 2017, following the merger of its separate corporate
  existence into Rangers Sub I, LLC on August 31, 2017; FelCor itself files no periodic
  reports after that date. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-17-056310, Form 15-12B]
- RLJ Lodging Trust (CIK 0001511337), the surviving/acquiring public filer, remains a
  continuing SEC registrant and has filed subsequent annual reports on Form 10-K,
  including one covering fiscal year 2021, filed February 24, 2022. [SRC: SEC accession 0001511337-22-000009, Form 10-K, FY2021]

## RLJ's consolidated portfolio record within the outcome window (combined-company scale)
- As of December 31, 2021 and December 31, 2020, RLJ owned 98 and 103 hotel properties,
  respectively; RLJ's Form 10-K notes that operating results are not comparable across
  periods because certain properties were acquired, sold, or otherwise disposed, and
  that the non-comparable set includes nine hotels sold or otherwise disposed and three
  hotels acquired between January 1, 2020 and December 31, 2021. [SRC: SEC accession 0001511337-22-000009, Form 10-K, FY2021]
- During the year ended December 31, 2021, RLJ recorded impairment losses of $144.8
  million in total, of which $5.9 million related to two hotel properties sold in May
  2021 and $138.9 million related to the DoubleTree Metropolitan New York City, which
  was sold in December 2021. [SRC: SEC accession 0001511337-22-000009, Form 10-K, FY2021]
- These portfolio-level and impairment figures describe RLJ's combined-company results
  as a whole; the FY2021 Form 10-K does not identify any specific hotel, disposition, or
  impairment as originating from the hotels acquired in the FelCor merger, nor does it
  present a segregated financial or operating disclosure for that acquired group. [SRC: SEC accession 0001511337-22-000009, Form 10-K, FY2021]

## Items sought but not found
- No source was located in which RLJ separately discloses a divestiture, impairment,
  brand conversion, or other outcome scalar specifically attributed to the hotels
  originally acquired from FelCor as a distinct, identifiable group within the
  ~2020-2022 outcome window. RLJ's FY2021 Form 10-K references to "FelCor" are limited
  to REIT-qualification tax history related to the acquisition and to an exhibit
  identifying a supplemental indenture assumed at closing, not to a business-trajectory
  disclosure. [SRC: SEC accession 0001511337-22-000009, Form 10-K, FY2021]
- Whether any of the specific hotels reported sold or impaired by RLJ during the outcome
  window (e.g., the DoubleTree Metropolitan New York City) were originally part of the
  39-hotel FelCor portfolio could not be determined from the filings reviewed. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- FelCor Lodging Trust Incorporated itself generated no post-closing public record: it
  deregistered on September 8, 2017 and files no periodic reports thereafter. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-17-056310, Form 15-12B]
- The acquirer, RLJ Lodging Trust, is a continuing public filer whose consolidated
  portfolio contracted from 103 to 98 hotels between year-end 2020 and year-end 2021 and
  which recorded $144.8 million of impairment losses in fiscal year 2021, but no filing
  reviewed separately discloses the post-close trajectory of the specific hotels
  acquired from FelCor. [SRC: SEC accession 0001511337-22-000009, Form 10-K, FY2021]
- Per the no-record convention, this case is coded **uncertain** on the outcome for the
  acquired business: the absence of a business-specific disclosure precludes a sourced
  determination of the realized 3-5-year trajectory of the specific hotels acquired from
  FelCor, even though the acquirer continues to be a public filer.

[SLICE END]
